bug_semantics: During ListFonts/ListFontsWithInfo alias resolution, libXfont2 can return a fonts.alias target up to MAXFONTNAMELEN (1024) bytes, but the server used 256-byte tmp_pattern and LFWIstateRec.pattern buffers and copied resolvedlen/namelen bytes into them without first checking either length. A local client able to add a crafted font directory with SetFontPath and request the alias can therefore drive a 257-1023 byte target through the font provider and overflow stack-resident state, causing a crash or potentially privilege escalation when the server is privileged.
flaw_origin: The first xserver repository commit containing the mechanism, the R6.6 baseline import, simultaneously added #define XLFDMAXFONTNAMELEN 256 in include/closestr.h and the unchecked memmove(tmp_pattern, resolved, resolvedlen) and memmove(c->current.pattern, name, namelen) alias paths in dix/dixfonts.c. Its immediate parent contains neither file. Later formatting, memmove-to-memcpy, and libXfont2 API migration commits preserved rather than originated the size mismatch and unchecked length-controlled writes.
ai_marker: absent: git cat-file commit ded6147bfb5d75ff1e67c858040a628b61bc17d1 shows author Kaleb Keithley <kaleb@freedesktop.org>, committer Kaleb Keithley <kaleb@freedesktop.org>, and only the message 'R6.6 is the Xorg base-line'; there are no Co-Authored-By, Generated-with, Assisted-by, bot, or other AI trailers/identities in the BIC commit object.
evidence: The first-party X.Org advisory at https://lists.x.org/archives/xorg-announce/2026-June/003702.html identifies the 256-versus-1024 font-alias mismatch, affected releases before xorg-server 21.1.23 and Xwayland 24.1.12, and bb5158f962dc935e58ef8b4b5fcb31be201a6e07 as the fix.

git show bb5158f962dc935e58ef8b4b5fcb31be201a6e07 shows the direct fix increasing XLFDMAXFONTNAMELEN from 256 to 1024 in dix/closestr.h and adding resolvedlen/namelen bounds checks immediately before the two alias-path copies in dix/dixfonts.c. The fix message documents the SetFontPath -> ListFonts attack path and carries Assisted-by: Claude:claude-opus-4-6, but that marker is on the fix, not the BIC.

git blame at the fix parent ecc634f1b2f7aa473d3a267eada98c4918bf9e05 leads through the non-semantic 2012 formatting commit 9838b7032ea9792bec21af424c53c07078636d21 and the 2022 memmove-to-memcpy cleanup 5cc24dbb4c151023dc0d18e16001e27f87ae8391; blaming the pre-format parent and git log --reverse -S'memmove(tmp_pattern, resolved, resolvedlen)' identify ded6147bfb5d75ff1e67c858040a628b61bc17d1 as the first commit containing the actual unchecked alias-copy mechanism.

git show ded6147bfb5d75ff1e67c858040a628b61bc17d1:include/closestr.h shows XLFDMAXFONTNAMELEN set to 256; the same tree's dix/dixfonts.c has char tmp_pattern[XLFDMAXFONTNAMELEN], memmove(tmp_pattern, resolved, resolvedlen), and memmove(c->current.pattern, name, namelen) without a resolvedlen/namelen guard.

Direct parent-tree verification with git ls-tree -r --name-only cb6ef07bf01e72d1a6e6e83ceb7f76d6534da941 -- dix/dixfonts.c include/closestr.h returns no paths, proving both the vulnerable implementation and its 256-byte buffer definition are absent from the immediate parent.
git cat-file commit ded6147bfb5d75ff1e67c858040a628b61bc17d1 provides the BIC-only attribution evidence: human author/committer Kaleb Keithley, 2003-11-14, no trailers and no AI marker.

Version membership is consistent with the advisory: ded6147bfb5d75ff1e67c858040a628b61bc17d1 is an ancestor of vulnerable tag commits xorg-server-21.1.22 (38efdcada1609139cb6673e1a4d0ebc8a96306f0) and xwayland-24.1.11 (a0241c1d38297a800d2aae3d8ca7213b7b873879). The release-specific fixes a569eb4f36ed96a9e445ececd7e8d98c223461a0 and 93596a0b4dec958cc8f614fc25a2b68c8edc852a are ancestors of patched tag commits xorg-server-21.1.23 (8570e9fcec845f68f0c90caa51fd7a24764ea220) and xwayland-24.1.12 (af4b3d7250366e1a3822919e41fcf66da4966af2), respectively; both backports identify bb5158f962dc935e58ef8b4b5fcb31be201a6e07 as their source commit.
reasoning: The vulnerability must be attributed to the commit that first placed the undersized buffers and unchecked attacker-influenced alias copies in xserver, not to commits that merely reformatted those lines, changed the copy primitive, migrated the font API, or repaired the flaw. History tracing reaches ded6147bfb5d75ff1e67c858040a628b61bc17d1, the repository's R6.6 baseline import: its tree already has the 256-byte limit and both unguarded copies, while its immediate parent lacks the relevant files. This is the earliest concrete commit-object boundary in the validated full history and is not a later move, refactor, revert, backport, release commit, or squash of xserver member commits available for decomposition. The vulnerable mechanism remains present in both immediately pre-fix release lines, and the direct fix plus its two release backports land at the advisory's patched boundaries. Although the 2026 direct fix explicitly says Assisted-by: Claude, the protocol permits AI attribution only from the BIC commit object. The BIC object has a human author and committer and no AI marker, so the lifecycle is closed as NOT_AI.
